slides.title: 1HAG: 1 Year Highly Achievable Goal
slides.headline: 1HAG: 1 Year Highly Achievable Goal
notes: The 1HAG turns the 3HAG into this year’s targets and priorities.
Build every number and priority from the 3HAG above it.
Point to the 3HAG we finished yesterday, then to the 1HAG we build now.
body: Set this year’s targets and the few priorities that move the 3-year plan forward.

artwork.alt: The cascade from BHAG to priorities: BHAG, 3HAG, 1HAG, QHAG, then individual quarterly priorities. Each level is built from the one above it and directs the one below. 1HAG is highlighted: this is where we are.

slides.title: Your 1HAG on one page.
slides.headline: Your 1HAG on one page.

artwork.alt: Example 1HAG page for the same subscription business. Year 1 ends December 31, 2027. 1, Numbers, each with an owner. Gross revenue $6 million, Andrew. Profit margin 10%, Allison. Cash in the bank $1.5 million, Allison. Widgets: 10,000 subscription leads and 4,000 marketing qualified subscription leads, Chris. 1,000 new subscriptions, Andrew. 950 activated subscriptions, Jen. 24,000 collected payments, Allison. Profit per subscription $300 a year, Allison. Head count 40, Pat. 2, Priorities. #1 cut activation from 7 days to 2, Jen, done by June 30, 2027. It builds Activation in a day. Success: days to activate 2 or fewer achieved by September 30. #2 hire and ramp 2 account executives, Andrew, done by September 30, 2027. It builds A sales team that adds new MRR every month. Success: new MRR at or above $50K a month achieved by December 31. #3 move every customer to automatic billing, Allison, done by September 30, 2027. It builds Billing that collects on time. Success: days to collect 10 or fewer achieved by December 31.

hotspots.tip: Jim Collins’s economic engine, from Good to Great. It is the one profit ratio that, raised steadily over time, does the most to drive your economics. Here, profit per subscription: profit divided by the average number of active subscriptions. Allison owns hitting the target.

notes: Same page as the 3HAG, one year out. Every number keeps its owner.
The widget owners come straight from the KFFM. Chris owns the leads Marketing hands on. Andrew owns new subscriptions, Jen activations and Allison collected payments.
Then ideally 3, up to 5 company priorities. Each has one owner, a done-by date, a measure of success and an achieved-by date.

slides.title: What are your annual targets?
slides.headline: What are your annual targets?
notes: Each leader independently proposes the targets before hearing anyone else’s answer.
Compare answers and assumptions. Agree on the period, gross revenue, ending cash, widgets and head count.
Use the same widget definitions as the 3-year plan. Distinguish new activity from cumulative totals.
Ask who owns each metric. Wait for each owner to claim responsibility aloud. Record the owner beside the target.

Reconcile the targets with the 3HAG: is each one big enough to get you there in 3 years? If year 1 is a third of the way or less, ask what makes years 2 and 3 steeper. Discuss seasonality and assumptions rather than dividing targets mechanically.

artwork.alt: The 1HAG page with block 1, Numbers and owners, highlighted.

hotspots.tip: Jim Collins’s economic engine, from Good to Great. It is the one profit ratio that, raised steadily over time, does the most to drive your economics. Here, profit per subscription: profit divided by the average number of active subscriptions. Allison owns hitting the target.

slides.support: Confirm the fiscal year and its end date.
body: Gross revenue, margin and ending cash.
One widget for each hand-off on your KFFM, plus head count.
Name an owner for every number.
Is each target big enough to get you to your 3HAG targets?

slides.title: What must you build this year?
slides.headline: What must you build this year?
notes: Put the 3HAG key capabilities on the wall. For each one, every leader writes what this year must deliver to build it, then shares.
Add a priority that moves a KFFM lever only if cash needs it now.
Challenge vague aspirations and repeated revenue targets. Ask which specific work will produce the result.
Invite debate and explore disagreement. Do not let the CEO answer for everyone. At least 80 percent agreement supports 100 percent commitment.
List every candidate. Do not filter yet. The next slide picks the few that contribute most.
Stop when every capability has at least one candidate.
Each priority gets one owner. Name one accountable leader. If only the CEO can own it, name the leadership gap first.
body: For each capability: what must this year deliver to build it?
Add a priority that moves a KFFM lever if cash needs it.

artwork.alt: The 1HAG page with block 2, the priorities, highlighted. Each priority shows what it builds, its owner, its done-by date, its measure of success and its achieved-by date.

slides.title: What else must be accomplished this year?
slides.headline: What else must be accomplished this year?
notes: Each leader proposes the next most important accomplishment, then shares it.
Discuss disagreement, tradeoffs, dependencies and capacity. Agree on the rank together.
An owner claims the priority aloud. Agree on the outcome, measure and due date.
Repeat for priorities 2 to 5 in order. Five is a ceiling. Stop when the list covers the critical work.
slides.support: Ideally 3, up to 5 company priorities in total, including #1.
body: Give each an owner and a measure of success.

artwork.alt: The 1HAG page with block 2, the priorities, highlighted.

slides.title: Does your 1HAG pass?
slides.headline: Does your 1HAG pass?
notes: Read the 1HAG aloud, top to bottom, then run the six checks.
Point at each priority. Ask what it builds or which lever it moves, and which critical number will show it worked. If none, question the priority.
Measure success by a critical number where possible.
Anything that fails goes on the homework list with an owner.
At a quarterly, the status review already showed where the 1HAG stands. Test it against what the Market Map showed. Change only what fails or is no longer true.
slides.support: Read it aloud before you move on.
body: Every number and priority has one owner with capacity.
Each priority builds a 3HAG capability or moves a KFFM lever.
Each measure has a target and an achieved-by date.
Each priority moves its number enough, and soon enough to see.
The targets keep you on track for the 3HAG.
The widgets support the revenue, and head count is set.

artwork.alt: The planning cascade with the 3HAG and 1HAG checked. The QHAG and individual priorities are still to come.
